title: OOM buffer checkpointing with rollback and probing fallback paths
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Under sustained high-throughput tails we observe recurrent OOM cascades where a single oversized batch or a long-dialog request exhausts GPU working set and forces an expensive global reclamation (full KV flush + batch drop). Existing soft-eviction strategies reduce frequency but still produce multi-request failures and noisy latency spikes.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, per-request "buffer checkpointing" and rollback mechanism that lets the serving runtime create micro-checkpoints of volatile in-GPU buffers (batch admission state, prefix KV deltas, allocated scratch arenas) and perform fast client-visible rollbacks or model-path probes instead of global eviction. Complement this with a probing-based fallback selector that tests cheaper model variants (quantized / smaller context) via short micro-probes before full failover, to avoid unnecessary quality loss.

Design summary:
- Admission contract: new request-level flag "checkpointable": runtime accepts a checkpointable request and will maintain at most N micro-checkpoints for it while in the batch queue. Non-checkpointable requests skip checkpoint flow (backwards-compatible).
- Checkpoint content: compressed delta of ephemeral allocations needed to rewind request progression (not full KV snapshot). For chat-like streams this is prefix-delta (token index -> delta entries) + small arena bitmap. Checkpoints are sized to remain under 2-4% of model GPU memory footprint and stored in a reserved checkpoint slab per-device.
- Rollback action: on OOM or heavy memory pressure the admission controller can roll back one or more in-flight checkpointed requests to their last checkpointed token, re-enqueue with reduced context or alternative model path, and release the in-flight ephemeral allocations. The calling client receives a structured retry response indicating rollback occurred and suggested retry parameters (e.g., trimmed_prefix=K, model_variant=redwood-small-quant).
- Probing fallback: before swapping a large set of inflight requests to a lower-cost model, the runtime runs micro-probes (3-6 short token generations across candidate variants) using spared micro-batches to measure p50 latency and soft quality signals (token-likelihood delta / confidence heuristics). If the probe indicates acceptable latency/quality tradeoffs, only then we route a subset of requests to that variant and progressively ramp.
- KV integration: checkpoint deltas reference minimal KV indices and patch operations; they are compatible with existing KV-lease invariant (we do not create persistent divergent KV states). If a rollback reduces prefix and replays on the same model, KV alignment is guaranteed via an idempotent replay path. If switched to a fallback model, we apply conservative KV coalescing and may fall back to contextless inference for the trimmed prefix.

APIs and telemetry:
- API: addition of request header / param checkpointable=true/false and optional target_fallbacks=[ids].
- Telemetry: counters for checkpoints_created, checkpoints_reused, rollbacks_triggered, probes_run, probe_success_rate, rollback_latency_penalty, and QoE delta (post-rollback quality metric vs baseline).

Safety & trade-offs:
- Checkpoints are intentionally lightweight to minimize memory tax; they cannot cover all allocation types (e.g., large embedding caches). For these, admission controller still prefers admission shaping or denylist.
- Rollbacks introduce complexity for exactly-once semantics for streamed outputs; we return a structured retry envelope instead of silently rewinding to avoid client confusion.
- Probing costs a small CPU/GPU budget; we limit probe rate and make it opt-in per-customer by default (can be enabled by SLA tier).

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Rollbacks reduce multi-request OOM failures by >= 70% in synthetic sustained tail test (see test-plan).
- Probe-based fallback selection avoids unnecessary model switches 90% of the time and reduces mean failover latency by >= 20% compared to blind fallback.
- Checkpoint slab contention remains < 5% of device memory under 95th percentile workload for internal stress tests.
- End-to-end client signal (structured retry) is implemented in the SDKs and documented in the API spec.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic sustained tail test: multi-request OOM failure rate reduced >= 70% with checkpoint+rollback enabled
Probe success rate: probing avoids full model fails in >= 90% of probe decisions in controlled A/B
Memory overhead: checkpoint slab consumption < 5% device memory at 95th percentile load
SDK/Protocol: structured retry envelope implemented and documented; clients can opt into automatic retry helpers in SDK
No regressions: existing non-checkpointed request P50 latency regression < 5% in canary
notes: Prototype idea came out of SRE incident 2026-01-18 where a single long-request caused three downstream batch evictions in a row
Prefer delta-only checkpoints vs full KV snapshots to keep memory tax low and avoid long serialization loops
We need to coordinate with Console team to surface rollback events in per-route dashboards and cost attribution
Security review: checkpoint slab is ephemeral in-GPU memory; still need to ensure no sensitive plaintext persists when using private deployments (add optional encrypted offload)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime flag `enable_checkpointing_v1`. 2) Internal canary (10% of traffic) with probe_rate=0.05 and checkpoint_limit=2. 3) Measure metrics for 48h, run safety checks, increase to 50% if green. 4) Gradual tenant opt-in and console toggle for SLA tiers. 5) Full enable with per-model fallback lists after 7d of stable metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint delta encoding/decoding and idempotent replay
Microbench: end-to-end rollback latency measured on p4d and a100 clusters
Chaos test: force OOM mid-batch and assert rollback path re-enqueues correctly and releases allocations
Bench: probe overhead measured with 50k probes and quality heuristics validated against human eval set
ops_runbook:
- Detection: Monitor rollbacks_triggered > 0 with spike in rollback_latency_penalty.
- Mitigation: Temporarily disable checkpointing flag if rollout exhibits slab saturation, increase checkpoint_purge frequency, or raise admission watermark.
- Recovery: If rollback rate remains high for >1h, scale dedicated pool and alert SRE.
- Post-mortem: attach checkpoints_created and probe logs to incident ticket for replay
